* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Deaf Smith County in the panhandle of Texas...

* WHEN...Until 245 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1148 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Up to 1 inch of rain has fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Hereford.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves due to
elevated surf. There is a risk of moderate coastal flooding
especially Monday and Tuesday.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Malibu Coast and
Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Moderate flooding of sea water is possibly over
some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
late morning high tide, including over beach parking lots,
bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is
likely. Isolated damage is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Coastal Flood Advisory products will
likely be needed for Monday and Tuesday.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves due to
elevated surf. Minor tidal overflows possible especially
Monday and Tuesday.

* WHERE...Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast, Santa Barbara
County Southeastern Coast and Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Pooling of sea water is possible around high tide at
beach and harbor areas (including Santa Barbara Harbor).
Enhanced beach erosion is also possible. No significant damage
is expected.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Socorro County in central New Mexico...

* Until 115 AM MDT.

* At 1022 PM MDT, trained weather spotters reported thunderstorms
producing heavy rain in northern Socorro. Up to 6 inches of rain
have fallen near and just west of the Socorro area. Additional
rainfall amounts up to 1.5 inches are possible in the warned area.
Flash flooding is already occurring.

FLASH FLOOD EMERGENCY for Socorro and Luis Lopez. This is a
PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION. SEEK HIGHER GROUND NOW!

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Trained spotters reported.

IMPACT...This is a PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION. SEEK HIGHER
GROUND NOW! Life threatening flash flooding of low water
crossings, small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Socorro, Escondida, Lemitar, San Antonio, Luis Lopez and Laborcita.

This includes the following highways...
Highway 60 between Mile Markers 122 and 138. Interstate 25 between
Mile Markers 139 and 158.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Jewell, KS; Mitchell, KS; Osborne, KS; Smith, KS
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWGID

The National Weather Service in Hastings has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Jewell County in north central Kansas...
Northwestern Mitchell County in north central Kansas...
Central Osborne County in north central Kansas...
Southeastern Smith County in north central Kansas...

* Until 515 AM CDT.

* At 1118 PM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
2 and 4 inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is
0.5 to 1.5 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2
inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing
or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Osborne, Downs, Mankato, Cawker City, Glen Elder, Jewell, Burr Oak,
Portis, Esbon, Ionia, Webber, Montrose and Lovewell State Park.

The heaviest rain amounts near 4 inches are from near Downs
northeastward into far southwest Jewell County.
